title: Applying, Approval and Plan Activation — PracticePay Patient Financing
content:
## Clauses

1. A PracticePay application is taken only at a provider whose enrollment status is active. The chosen plan must be offered for the provider's specialty.
2. The applicant must meet the plan's minimum credit score; a parent or guardian may apply as the borrower for a minor patient or for a pet's treatment when the plan allows a responsible party. The approved amount lies between the plan's minimum and maximum financed amounts.
3. The approval stays usable until the approval expiration date, the approval date plus the plan's approval validity days.
4. The provider's treatment charge activates the plan only when the current date is no later than the approval expiration date, the approval date plus the plan's approval validity days. The validity period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the approval date, and a charge submitted on the last day is in time.
5. An approval not used in time expires. The charge may not exceed the approved amount and may not be below the plan's minimum financed amount; a plan carries the plan's number of treatment charges per plan (one charge).
6. A treatment charge is financed only on a plan in active status, the status its activation gives it.
7. On activation the purchase date is the date of service, the promotional period ends the plan's promotional months calendar months after the purchase date (the day before the same day of that month; the last day of the month when that day does not exist), the first due date is the first due day at least 25 calendar days after the purchase date, and the monthly payment follows the plan's payment method.

The minimum credit score, financed amounts, eligible specialties, approval validity days, promotional months and the other per-plan figures are those of the entry-requirements and plan schedules for PracticePay Patient Financing. Every condition above is judged on Larkspur's records: the provider's enrollment status and specialty, the plan's approval date and its status.

## Plan statuses along the way

An application is applied, then approved or declined. An approval becomes active when the provider submits the treatment charge in time, or expires when it does not. An active plan ends paid off, cancelled (when the provider refunds the full financed amount) or charged off.

## Boundary of the approval period (hypothetical)

For a plan whose approval validity is 60 days, counting starts on the day after the approval date:

| Day the provider submits the charge | Outcome |
|---|---|
| the 60th calendar day after the approval date | in time; the plan activates |
| the 61st calendar day after the approval date | too late; the approval has expired |

## First due date and promotional end (hypothetical)

- A purchase on 10 March with a due day of the 5th: 5 April is 26 days later and is at least 25 days after, so the first due date is 5 April.
- A purchase on 20 March with a due day of the 5th: 5 April is 16 days later, fewer than 25, so the first due date is 5 May.
- A 6-month promotional period on a purchase dated 10 March ends on 9 September, the day before the same day six calendar months later.
